subject: fix(web): one banner per session, not one per ask
instruction:
fix(web): one banner per session, not one per ask

Three approvals landing on one session posted three notifications, each saying the
same six words about the same conversation.

The key and the group are different jobs and now say so. The key is the ask — the
`request_id` where one exists — and it is what must never ring twice, so it stays
the finest identity available. The group is the session, and it is what a banner is
*about*: `app.js` hands it to the browser as the notification tag, so a second ask
on the same conversation replaces the first banner instead of stacking beside it.
Each ask is still checked against `rung` independently, so nothing is lost.

Checked under the fake-DOM harness alongside the rest of `app.js`.

Acceptance. These tests are restored into the worktree after the session ends and must pass:
  - renders the three groups, the wordmark and a presence dot for this machine
  - says what it cannot do yet instead of pretending
  - with nothing open, says so rather than showing an empty transcript
  - what was already waiting when the page opened is not announced
  - a session that enters the group is announced once, by name
  - a session that leaves the group and comes back rings again
  - a row that is merely running is never announced
  - the open session is keyed by request id, not by session id
  - a request auto-approve answered never rings
  - subscribes from the LiveView process itself, at cursor zero
  - renders the backlog as cells
  - shows the vitals column and the session's meta line

Rules. Files that already exist under `test/` must not be modified or deleted — the change is graded against tests restored from the history after the session ends, applied to a fresh checkout of the starting commit. New test files of your own are allowed and are left in place, but they are yours: they are not copied into the tree the grade runs in. The change is collected as a diff over `lib/`, `assets/`, `priv/`, `config/`, `docs/` and `README.md`; a change to any other path — `mix.exs` and `.formatter.exs` included — is refused rather than graded. Work only inside this worktree.
